mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows Alloy to find audit entries where a clinician accesses a patient record with Permitted outcome despite not being on the active care team. The assertion CareTeamGating checks this invariant and will fail when the fact is removed and a violating instance is injected.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamViolation { some disj ae: AuditEntry, ctm: CareTeamMembership | ae.user = ctm.clinician and ae.patient = ctm.patient and ae.accessType = ReadRecord and ae.outcome = Permitted and ctm.status = "ended" }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows clinical notes to exist without corresponding audit entries. The AlwaysOnAudit assertion checks that every note has a matching audit entry and will fail when this fact is removed and a note without an audit is injected.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMissing { some n: ClinicalNote | no ae: AuditEntry | ae.noteId = n.noteId and ae.accessType = AddNote and ae.outcome = Permitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact leaves the permission matrix empty or unconstrained, violating the least-privilege principle. Injecting that HospitalAdministrator can ReadRecord (which is not in the allowed matrix) causes LeastPrivilege to fail.
Removing this fact allows non-administrators to perform ListAudit. Injecting an audit entry where a clinical role performs ListAudit with Permitted outcome causes the assertion to fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_ListAuditNonAdmin { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.accessType = ListAudit and ae.outcome = Permitted and ae.userRole in (Doctor + Nurse + Pharmacist + ClinicalAdmin) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows administrators to author notes, violating the append-only clinical-notes invariant. Injecting a note authored by HospitalAdministrator causes the assertion to fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AdminAuthorNote { some n: ClinicalNote | n.authorRole = HospitalAdministrator }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to have incorrect authorisation basis values. Injecting an audit with mismatched basis (e.g., a successful ReadRecord with PatientNotFoundBasis instead of CareTeamMemberBasis) causes the assertion to fail.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_WrongBasis { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.accessType = ReadRecord and ae.outcome = Permitted and ae.authorisationBasis != CareTeamMemberBasis }
